interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative prognosis is favorable based on the documented surgical findings. Key positive factors include a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) diagnosis, negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and no lymph node metastasis. These findings suggest a low-risk pathological profile. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 5.9. The absence of documented biopsy-to-prostatectomy differences prevents assessment of potential histological discrepancies. Nodal status was documented as negative. The primary uncertainty in the prognosis stems from the lack of documented postoperative PSA and subsequent follow-up data, which is critical for trajectory assessment. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent changes would significantly revise this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 84.76 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 63.57–105.95 months; its coverage has not been validated.
